Color sequences and scales

Source: R/zz-gen-colors.R
px_colors.Rd

The named color sequences and scales of plotly.py's plotly.colors module: px_colors$qualitative (discrete color sequences, e.g. Plotly, D3, Set1), px_colors$sequential (e.g. Viridis, Plasma, Blues), px_colors$diverging (e.g. RdBu) and px_colors$cyclical (e.g. Twilight). Each is a character vector of colors; use rev() to reverse one.

Usage

px_colors

Format

A list of four named lists of character vectors.

Details

Sequential, diverging and cyclical scales can also be given by name (case-insensitive, with "_r" appended to reverse) to any colorscale property, e.g. marker = list(colorscale = "viridis_r").

Examples

names(px_colors$qualitative)
#>  [1] "Alphabet" "Antique"  "Bold"     "D3"       "Dark2"    "Dark24"  
#>  [7] "G10"      "Light24"  "Pastel"   "Pastel1"  "Pastel2"  "Plotly"  
#> [13] "Prism"    "Safe"     "Set1"     "Set2"     "Set3"     "T10"     
#> [19] "Vivid"   
px_colors$qualitative$Plotly
#>  [1] "#636EFA" "#EF553B" "#00CC96" "#AB63FA" "#FFA15A" "#19D3F3" "#FF6692"
#>  [8] "#B6E880" "#FF97FF" "#FECB52"
rev(px_colors$sequential$Viridis)
#>  [1] "#fde725" "#b5de2b" "#6ece58" "#35b779" "#1f9e89" "#26828e" "#31688e"
#>  [8] "#3e4989" "#482878" "#440154"
